text: Why does two x squared plus three x squared equal five x squared? Let's make the symbols visible.
Take a square with side length x, where x is positive. Its area is x squared.
Here are two such squares, and three more. Every tile has exactly the same area: x squared.
Bring them together. Count five identical tiles. We changed how many we collected, not the area of each tile.
So, two x squared plus three x squared is two plus three, times x squared. That is five x squared.
This is the distributive law. Add the coefficients, and keep the shared variable part unchanged. The identity holds for every real x.
Addition keeps these terms as x squared. Multiplying x squared by x squared is different: that gives x to the fourth.
Your turn. What is four x squared plus two x squared? Explain what changes, and what stays the same.
Six x squared. Four plus two gives six; x squared stays unchanged. Like terms combine because their variable parts match.
